As long as they methodically tightened the noose, capturing the target was inevitable.Sarah understood this reality and didn’t waste time on futile maneuvers. Instead, wielding a high-molecular claw in one hand and a Negative Energy Blade in the other, she dug downward at maximum speed.
The fastest method would have been to activate a Negative Energy Shield beneath her feet. With sufficient energy, she could even reach the planet’s core. However, this method was too energy-intensive, and she couldn’t sustain it for more than a few seconds. Excessive energy consumption would render her other abilities unusable, which was unwise given the circumstances.
Thus, she didn’t even employ dual Negative Energy Blades for digging, aiming to conserve energy. However, when it came to excavation, the Negative Energy Blade wasn’t significantly more effective than the high-molecular claw. Eventually, Sarah found that using both claws together was more efficient and energy-saving.
With less energy expenditure, switching to dual claws nearly halted her energy consumption. Meanwhile, the small Dark Energy Furnace within her worked at full capacity to replenish her reserves.
“She’s stalling. Order the frontline units to stop dawdling and capture the target immediately.”
“The Burrowing Worms below have gone berserk! At this rate, it won’t take them long to consume the entire safe soil layer.” The “safe soil layer” referred to areas free of X-576 radiation contamination. For Burrowing Worms, products of a standard biological template, the radiation boundary was an insurmountable forbidden zone.
However, their task was complete once they hollowed out the area outside the forbidden zone and sank it deeper underground. Other specialized units would handle the rest.
“I believe we need to detonate another X-576!”
“I disagree. As we’ve already discussed, once those Burrowing Worms are killed and lose their structural support, the target area will collapse. In that scenario, the target’s chances of escape would increase significantly.”
“Exactly. We’ve already located the target and surrounded her. Our priority now should be to capture her as soon as possible without causing further complications.”
“But this leaves us too passive. The Swarm could trigger the target area’s collapse at any moment. Detonating an X-576 would give us more control.”
“Hmph, what control? Once it collapses, who knows what the Swarm has prepared below? Can you guarantee we’ll still maintain control in that situation?”
“Indeed. If that happens, the battlefield’s scope will expand several times over. Our current forces aren’t sufficient to cover such a vast area, let alone with only two days left.”
“Enough. Look at this!”
After activating her Negative Energy Blade, its unique energy fluctuations were easily detected by the Ji race’s radars. Even after switching to dual claws, the vibrations from her digging still revealed her position on other instruments.
“The target is moving downward!”
“What are those fools doing? Selina? Selina? Quickly calculate a route and have those idiots intercept the target!”
At this moment, Sarah was fully immersed in her digging, momentarily relishing the joy once experienced by the Overlord—a spiritual resonance, albeit short-lived, as the Ji race interrupted it.
Under Selina’s coordination, K2N9 units swiftly reached designated positions, cutting off the frantically digging Swarm Empress.
“Your Majesty, don’t resist. You’re surrounded. Surrender now to avoid further suffering.”
“Yes, Your Majesty, we merely wish to invite you for further dialogue to enhance our mutual understanding and resolve any past misunderstandings.”
“Please, Your Majesty, come with us.”
Though no direct confrontation occurred, the Ji race’s attempts at persuasion echoed through the soil via loudspeakers. While these taunts held little inherent meaning, they weren’t entirely useless to Sarah.
Her echolocation system activated fully, utilizing the noise from the loudspeakers to map her surroundings and the Ji forces’ distribution in her mind.
Leveraging the Swarm Network, Sarah’s computational ability matched that of artificial intelligence. She quickly devised the most suitable escape route.
However, her position was transparent to the Ji side. Based on her movements, Selina recalculated new encirclement paths for the numerous Ji soldiers and metallic constructs.
In response, Sarah adjusted her plans in real-time based on the Ji forces’ changes. Thus, even before physical contact, a battle of computational prowess had already begun.

chapters.title: Chapter 739: Consumption
chapters.content:
The computational battle between the two sides didn’t last long, as the encirclement was shrinking at an alarming rate. In just a short while, Sarah found herself with no room to evade and was forced to engage.
Several K2N9 units charged toward Sarah without slowing down. The Ji race now had unwavering faith in the Swarm Empress’s custom armor, believing that such collisions wouldn’t harm her. Thus, their attacks became far less cautious and much more aggressive.
While these collisions couldn’t damage Sarah, they effectively hindered her movements and slowed her escape. Once surrounded and her energy depleted, most of her high-tech systems would be rendered useless, leaving her with only her superhuman physical abilities—insufficient for escape.
Fortunately, Sarah had already accumulated a significant amount of energy since earlier. Her specially customized body boasted numerous functions and came equipped with five energy storage organs. The resources consumed by this single small frame were enough to construct over a hundred Dark Energy Furnaces capable of powering Primordial bodies.
Facing the charging K2N9s, Sarah knew this wasn’t the time to conserve energy. Dual Negative Energy Blades extended, and with a few swift swings, she dismantled two K2N9s.
Shoving the broken metal parts aside, Sarah rushed out along the path one of the K2N9s had taken. This position was already surrounded, and continuing to dig downward would be suicidal. She needed to disrupt the Ji forces’ formation first.
The Ji soldiers following the K2N9s hadn’t expected such close contact with the Swarm Empress. However, this moment of “honor” was quickly interrupted by the alarm from their personal systems. Selina dutifully performed her duty, unaffected by irrelevant emotions.
Though Selina’s warning was timely, the proximity between the two sides was too close. When Sarah’s body erupted with a sonic boom, it signaled the end of the skirmish.
There was no need to waste precious energy using Negative Energy Blades on these minor threats. The Negative Energy Blade on her right arm retracted, replaced instantly by a High-Molecular Blade.
Though the Ji soldiers’ protective suits offered some resistance to the High-Molecular Blade, Sarah’s speed amplified its attack power. In the blink of an eye, several Ji soldiers met the same fate as the K2N9s.However, this was the Ji race’s home turf. Behind the tunnels, countless Ji soldiers were still converging. Sarah turned back to rummage through the fallen Ji soldiers, retrieving their high-explosive grenades. Most of their weapons were identity-bound, requiring specific unlocking methods that outsiders couldn’t use even if they obtained them.
Thankfully, high-explosive grenades required no such authentication and were quite handy. Based on feedback from her echolocation system, some Ji squads had already begun pursuing her from behind.
Removing the safety rings, Sarah hurled two grenades with enhanced strength from her bio-armor. They screamed through the air before detonating with two thunderous blasts.
Though the grenades’ loud explosions couldn’t harm the K2N9s or the armored Ji soldiers, they were sufficient to destabilize the already fragile tunnel structure.
A few more grenades were thrown, detonating at different points along the tunnel, sealing off the retreat route. This temporarily delayed the encirclement’s closure.
During this brief reprieve, Sarah could focus on dealing with the enemies in front of her.
After Sarah swiftly dispatched one K2N9 and several Ji soldiers, the remaining Ji forces grew more cautious. Instead of blindly charging, they positioned two K2N9s as shields while other Ji soldiers attacked Sarah from a distance.
Sarah’s overwhelming performance had an unintended consequence: the Ji forces became overly confident in her defenses, resorting to firing blunt-nosed projectiles at her.
Though purely physical attacks, the projectiles’ mass and velocity gave them considerable impact. If struck, even her bio-armor absorbing most of the energy, Sarah would still be knocked flying by the residual force.
In such narrow tunnels, being knocked back meant the subsequent blunt-nosed projectiles would act like crowd-control skills with no cooldown, rendering Sarah unable to rise.
Though fast, the blunt-nosed projectiles were still trackable thanks to Sarah’s custom body granting her superior dynamic vision. Combined with her extraordinary reflexes, she could confidently evade them in open terrain, potentially retreating or even counterattacking.
Unfortunately, this was a narrow underground tunnel. The unique terrain significantly diminished her agility advantage. Though she could see every projectile’s trajectory, calculating an evasion path was impossible.
Fortunately, Sarah had other abilities. The Negative Energy Shield—a near game-breaking skill at this stage—could render her invincible as long as her energy reserves lasted.
Although Sarah’s energy reserves were relatively ample, sustaining the Negative Energy Shield for prolonged periods was unsustainable. She was still some distance from true invincibility.
However, Sarah had her own energy-saving tricks. A stronger Negative Energy output and control system, supported by the Swarm Network’s infinite computational power, allowed her to perform precise operations.
Dodging two blunt-nosed projectiles, rolling away from another five, and leaping backward to avoid three more, Sarah was eventually cornered with no room to maneuver.
Facing five incoming blunt-nosed projectiles, Sarah stood her ground. At the last possible moment, a thin layer of energy shield appeared in front of her. Without sparking, the shield erased the projectiles into nothingness, consuming a small portion of Sarah’s energy in the process.
The Negative Energy Shield’s defense mechanism was peculiar—it treated all matter equally. Whether dark energy bombs, high-quality alloys, or ordinary mud and sand, anything that touched it was mercilessly erased.
The energy consumption for each interaction wasn’t significantly different. This was why Sarah avoided using the Negative Energy Shield for digging; the dense soil layers would deplete her energy reserves like a deflating balloon in a very short time.
By her calculations, her energy reserves could erase approximately twenty tons of positive-energy material. While seemingly substantial, it would only allow her to descend about a hundred meters into the soil before becoming a powerless husk.
However, against blunt-nosed projectiles, even standing still, she could exhaust an entire Ji battalion’s ammunition quota.
But to endure longer on the battlefield, Sarah had to be meticulous in her energy management.

chapters.title: Chapter 740: Solution
chapters.content:
Once the battle began, there were too many areas requiring energy consumption. Abilities like electromagnetic acceleration and electromagnetic force, though seemingly low in energy expenditure, accumulated significant consumption when continuously activated and frequently used.
Next, high-molecular blades and armor repair required energy to support the bio-armor’s proliferation. Finally, the Negative Energy Blade was a major energy consumer. Sarah had to reserve sufficient energy to activate this ability at critical moments to cleave through obstacles.
Similarly, the Negative Energy Shield needed to be activated at key moments to block unavoidable attacks.
Thus, although Sarah’s energy reserves were relatively ample for now, meticulous energy management was essential. Having energy reserves meant fighting without panic.
However, the rapid toggling of the Negative Energy Shield, while conserving energy to the utmost, also exposed her limitations.
“Her energy reserves aren’t sufficient.”
“The Negative Energy Shield consumes too much energy. Prepare some targeted attack methods on the frontline!”
The blunt-nosed projectiles couldn’t stop Sarah’s advance. Though her speed had slowed considerably, it was only relative. To the Ji soldiers, Sarah was still as fast as lightning. Without the aid of combat-assisted targeting systems, their naturally evolved vision couldn’t track Sarah’s movements.
Taking slightly longer than before, Sarah eliminated two K2N9s and several Ji soldiers blocking her path, then rummaged for more high-explosive grenades, collapsing the tunnel behind her before continuing forward.
Perhaps searching for grenades took some time; Sarah hadn’t run twenty meters when she encountered another barrage of blunt-nosed projectiles. By now, Sarah was well-versed in dealing with such attacks, dodging most projectiles and using the Negative Energy Shield to block the unavoidable few.Just as Sarah planned to eliminate the obstructing Ji squad like before, the number of blunt-nosed projectiles suddenly decreased, which wasn’t good news for Sarah.
Following closely, a disgusting liquid was sprayed toward her. From its airborne trajectory, Sarah recognized it immediately and quickly retreated a few steps backward.
Indeed, the liquid was extremely viscous, sticking wherever it landed with strong adhesive properties—essentially, a super-strong glue.
It seemed the Ji race had found a method to counter Sarah’s Negative Energy Shield. The thick streams of glue couldn’t be evaded by mere agility.
Moreover, once hit, aside from the unpleasantness, the glue’s strong adhesion provided excellent control. Once entangled, escaping would be nearly impossible.
As for neutralizing these attacks with the Negative Energy Shield, it wasn’t impossible, but the energy consumption would be astronomical. Even if she managed to eliminate this squad, the Ji race had likely deployed numerous such teams around the area. Sarah estimated that if she directly resisted these attacks, she could take out at most five squads before running out of energy, leaving her immobilized and sealed like an amber specimen.
However, this glue-spraying attack had its pros and cons. While it hindered Sarah’s movement significantly, it also blocked the Ji team’s own route since it lacked a “teammate-friendly mode.” The passage clogged by the glue similarly locked down the Ji soldiers’ movement.
At this point, the firing of blunt-nosed projectiles had ceased because the passage was already blocked; the projectiles couldn’t reach through. Frankly, these glue attacks were easy to evade since they lacked homing capabilities. After the Ji soldiers launched their attack, Sarah simply retreated slightly, resulting in a glue wall forming between them.
Though it affected both parties, the Ji race aimed to restrict Sarah’s mobility, making this situation more advantageous for them.
Additionally, the Ji race suddenly realized that this gelatinous attack had other uses.
“Send more J-Z-901 solution reserves to the frontlines.”
“What?”
“I’ve discovered we can use J-Z-901 to reinforce the ground. If we glue the entire area together and attach a few stabilizing devices, even if the Swarm excavates underneath, what difference does it make?”
“Great idea!”
The Ji soldiers had a wide variety of weapons and equipment. There were seven or eight types of conventional grenades and over twenty special types. Ammunition options were even more extensive, along with various firearm modules and auxiliary devices. Even with the Ji soldiers’ high standard payload capacity, not everything could be accommodated.
The J-Z-901 solution and its accompanying launchers were among the rarest items, rarely used under most circumstances. In a standard Ji squad, perhaps only one or two members carried this equipment.
When two or three squads formed a platoon, their J-Z-901 solution and launcher configurations sufficed to impede Sarah’s escape but were far from enough to seal off the entire area.
However, there was plenty of this solution aboard the warships. Upon receiving orders, Selina directed various machines to package and deliver the specified materials. However, because J-Z-901 was so obscure and not on the standard delivery list, the preparation process took a few extra minutes compared to regular supplies.
The delivery and landing also required time, plus transportation to the underground battlefield. Even adding up these scattered durations, Sarah didn’t have much time left.
Sarah was unaware of the Ji race’s plans, but her current situation was already unfavorable. Fortunately, the area sealed by the gelatinous solution was extremely sturdy, requiring even K2N9s a long time to penetrate.
With the path ahead blocked and the rear collapsed, Sarah suddenly realized this might be a good opportunity to resume digging downward. Extending her high-molecular claws, Sarah embarked on her digging journey again.
Because the high-molecular claws were generated by the bio-armor, they could change shape freely. They transformed into sharp blades for attacks and into robust digging claws when excavating.
These claws incorporated features of digging appendages, being large and curved, making excavation highly effective. Combined with the strength and sensitivity granted by the bio-armor and the almost unparalleled physique of her insectoid body, Sarah’s digging speed was exceptionally fast.
Sarah’s actions were soon detected by the Ji race. Based on this, Selina adjusted the Ji squad’s encirclement routes. With the shrinking encirclement, she had more teams to deploy, making the encirclement tighter.
After digging downward for over thirty meters, Sarah stopped. Her echolocation system showed enemies approaching from almost every direction—above, below, front, back, left, and right.
However, at this moment, the Ji commander sent new instructions to Selina.

chapters.title: Chapter 741: Collapse
chapters.content:
The Ji commanders’ orders conflicted with their previous strategy. Initially, they aimed to capture the Swarm Empress as quickly as possible to avoid other variables.
However, upon the introduction of the J-Z-901 solution, they discovered a better option. If they reinforced this area with the gelatinous solution and added stabilizing devices, even if the ground beneath collapsed, this region would remain in place. Thus, the Swarm’s long-planned scheme would fail.
Yet, the encirclement had already shrunk significantly, and the J-Z-901 solution was still en route. To avoid excessively provoking Sarah and forcing the Swarm to trigger a collapse prematurely, the commanders decided to slow the attack temporarily. With just ten minutes, they could complete the initial soil reinforcement.
But this new plan was issued too late. Even though every Ji soldier was an excellent actor, with the encirclement already so tight, it was impossible to naturally delay for ten minutes without arousing suspicion.
Thus, some rather comical situations arose on the battlefield. For instance, Ji soldiers fled from combat for the first time, or they preemptively sealed passages with the gelatinous solution before even encountering Sarah.
These actions were too clumsy. Sarah keenly noticed the anomaly, realizing that a new variable must have emerged to cause these seemingly absurd situations.
Although the Ji fleet held the advantage in the planet’s near-orbit, the Swarm fleet hadn’t been completely eradicated. Moreover, numerous covert reconnaissance units within the planet were continuously being deployed, keeping the Ji race’s actions under constant surveillance.
The various airdropped packages launched from orbit were key surveillance targets. The Ji race had countermeasures; they understood the Swarm’s characteristics—all inconspicuous creatures might be Swarm spies.
Adhering to the principle of “better safe than sorry,” the Ji race dispatched countless miniature drones to eliminate all visible non-allied living organisms within the target area.
These thumb-sized drones could access more complex terrains to search for any possible targets. Equipped with three-centimeter-long beam-type guns, they conducted the first round of cleanup.When encountering targets they couldn’t clear, they marked them, and soon after, appropriate armed machines, under Selina’s command, arrived to eliminate the threats.
However, due to their size, these miniature drones couldn’t carry highly precise large instruments, limiting their detection capabilities. While they easily overwhelmed native wildlife, they struggled against Swarm reconnaissance units with both invisibility and mimicry abilities.
To minimize the Swarm’s hiding environments, the Ji race even set fire to clear all vegetation within a 300-kilometer radius. Though this indeed allowed them to discover and eliminate many Swarm units, numerous survivors continued fulfilling their duties.
Thus, when the packages containing J-Z-901 solution landed, these items, requiring special containers, immediately caught the Swarm’s attention.
By cross-referencing the obtained information, the Swarm quickly deduced what these packages were and easily guessed the Ji race’s intentions.
“Commander, the Swarm is on the move. Their Burrowing Worms are shifting positions.”
“Damn, our plan has been discovered! There are still spies we haven’t eliminated!”
“It’s normal. The Swarm has operated on that planet for so long; we can’t clear all their setups in a short time.”
“What now?”
“Proceed with the original plan. Let’s see who acts faster. Order the frontline teams to execute Plan B.”
“No problem, I hope it works.”
Large barrels of J-Z-901 solution were carried by transport robots, which sped toward the underground battlefield through the tunnels. These transport robots were equipped with anti-gravity systems, resembling flying carpets with mechanical arms, making them ideal for transportation tasks in certain environments.
Despite the Ji race’s efficient transport, the underground battlefield began to tremble. Numerous Burrowing Worms, acting as the foundation, departed, leaving the battlefield increasingly suspended. Under its own gravity, chunks of soil continuously disintegrated and fell downward.
Such extensive land movement caused each tremor to trigger massive disasters. The capillary-like tunnels surrounding the battlefield suffered first, with many collapsing successively.
The transport tunnels connecting to the surface were among them. Some transport convoys were merely cut off by collapsed soil layers, while others were directly buried.
Ultimately, only thirty percent of the transport convoy reached the designated position within the allotted time. By then, the situation was akin to a natural disaster—there was no time to equip their soldiers, let alone reinforce the soil structure.
Moreover, the Ji race faced more than just this one piece of bad news. After shifting positions, the Burrowing Worms below didn’t leave but instead charged resolutely toward the upper battlefield.
“They’re trying to detonate the high-explosive mines! Accelerate the battlefield collapse!”
These massive auxiliary units couldn’t effectively breach the radiation layer surrounding the battlefield, yet they proceeded regardless. This abnormal behavior led the Ji commanders to immediately deduce their intent.
Weapons previously intended to defend against Burrowing Worms suddenly became accomplices to the Swarm’s plan. This strategic blunder left the faces of several commanders and advisors who proposed it looking rather grim.
“Order the soldiers to accelerate, Selina, prepare the traction chains!”
Continuous thunderous explosions echoed underground. The immensely powerful high-explosive bombs not only killed and injured the Burrowing Worms but also collapsed the last solid soil layer supporting the battlefield.
Some fragments were over ten meters in diameter and weighed dozens of tons, while smaller ones were only fingernail-sized. A vast amount of rubble and soil plunged downward into the dark abyss.
The unstable foundation intensified the battlefield’s tremors, causing cracks to appear on the ground. Ji soldiers in the tunnels activated flight mode, but it was futile. The falling soil layers would drag them down unless they could escape mid-fall, otherwise, they’d face the Swarm forces below.
Some soldiers pulled out high-explosive grenades, holding them in hand. The shock from these grenades would be significantly reduced by their protective suits, ensuring even close-range explosions wouldn’t harm them. However, the grenades could create an opening for soldiers to escape when the surrounding soil layers detached. Even if they escaped the falling debris, they constantly dodged the falling mud and stones from above, which was far preferable to facing the Swarm’s encirclement.

chapters.title: Chapter 742: Struggle
chapters.content:
Sarah Kerrigan, trapped in the encirclement, naturally noticed the battlefield’s changes and realized that the rescue plan had been set into motion. To increase her chances of escape, she needed to take a more proactive approach.
The five energy storage organs began outputting energy as a Negative Energy Shield suddenly appeared beneath Sarah’s feet, instantly erasing the soil it touched.
Without any support, Sarah’s body continued to fall. The Negative Energy Shield beneath her feet continuously made contact with new layers of soil and rocks, erasing them as if she were riding an invisible elevator. Sarah plummeted downward at a speed several times faster than before.
Meanwhile, her energy reserves depleted rapidly, like a balloon with a large hole. Ideally, Sarah should have delayed for a bit longer, waiting for the lower soil layers to collapse and reduce the distance to the underground open area. This would allow her to conserve more energy for potential emergencies. However, the Ji race had already preemptively countered this by covertly reinforcing the soil beneath her feet.
The Ji teams surrounding Sarah numbered over a hundred. While their J-Z-901 gel solution couldn’t reinforce the entire battlefield, pooling their resources was more than sufficient to reinforce the area around and beneath Sarah.
From the start, the Ji race knew that reinforcing the entire battlefield wouldn’t succeed. Thus, hidden within this plan were other contingencies.
They didn’t need to reinforce the whole battlefield—only Sarah’s location mattered. Their earlier actions were merely misdirection to throw off the Swarm’s strategy.
“Stop her!” Although Plan B was essentially successful, compared to Plan A, the reinforced area of Plan B was much smaller, meaning a lower margin for error.
They had to confine Sarah within this area before her energy was depleted; otherwise, all their previous efforts would be in vain.
Sarah understood this point, which is why she opted for the fastest method to leave. However, the Ji race wouldn’t let her escape easily. During their earlier skirmishes, they had secretly reinforced nearly a hundred meters of soil beneath her feet. What seemed like a short distance—Sarah could traverse it in less than a second at her supersonic speed—now felt like an insurmountable chasm.J-Z-901 gel solution had a particularly nasty characteristic: the side in contact with objects would rapidly solidify, reaching hardness comparable to some mid-ring civilizations warship alloys.
This hardness allowed it to withstand a few strikes from high-molecular blades. Don’t underestimate this slight difference—cutting through in one strike versus two or three represented a significant increase in physical and energy consumption.
The non-adhering side of J-Z-901 remained highly viscous. Each strike of the high-molecular blade would get partially stuck in the gel, increasing the weapon’s weight and dulling its edge, making it extremely difficult to handle.
Thus, when the ground beneath her consisted entirely of a mixture of soil, rocks, and J-Z-901, Sarah was forced to expand the Negative Energy Shield beneath her feet to create enough space to avoid contact with the surrounding mud-gel mixture.
The additional energy drain from this expanded shield wasn’t to be underestimated; calculations showed Sarah would lose at least thirty percent of her descent distance. This development worried her, as she still didn’t know the thickness of the soil beneath her. If it exceeded a hundred meters, she might genuinely be trapped here.
At this moment, the Ji race deployed another contingency. A type of ammunition completely opposite to the blunt-nosed projectiles, these sharp-tipped, elongated bullets possessed extraordinary penetration power. Fired from specially enhanced firearms, they could traverse hundreds of meters of soil, even penetrating over a hundred meters of gel-soil. Within fifty meters, they still retained considerable lethality.
Based on Selina’s calculated lead, Ji soldiers began firing fiercely at the unseen Sarah. Though each squad carried only a small number of these special armor-piercing rounds, it was more than sufficient to intercept Sarah.
Bullets penetrated the soil layers from all directions, accurately striking the falling Sarah. With no room to dodge, she could only endure the hits.
Although the gel-soil had absorbed most of the bullets’ power, leaving insufficient force to breach her bio-armor, their kinetic energy still destabilized her body.
In this situation, she needed to exert more effort to maintain balance.
However, the barrage was overwhelming, and without any foothold, despite her best efforts, her body occasionally brushed against the surrounding walls. After a few instances, her body was coated with a thick layer of J-Z-901 gel-soil mixture.
Additionally, as the armor-piercing bullets traversed the gel-soil, they inevitably picked up some J-Z-901 gel. Upon contact with her body, there was a chance they would adhere, increasing her contact surface.
Back and forth, Sarah’s body became encased in a thick layer of J-Z-901 gel-soil, trapping her in the pipe, immobilized. Left with no choice, she activated the Negative Energy Shield at full power, creating a circle around her body to erase these burdens.
But not long after she resumed her descent, the same situation recurred, forcing her to repeat the action. This greatly slowed her fall and, more importantly, multiplied her energy consumption. She no longer had enough energy to traverse this special gel prison.
“That’s it; she definitely doesn’t have enough energy to finish this journey!”
“Is the gel prison’s stabilization complete?”
“It’s been done for a while. Even if the land where this battlefield is located collapses entirely, this area will remain in its original position.”
“Good. Now prepare to capture her. We’ve spent too much time here.”
“What about our soldiers who fell below?”
“After capturing the target, try to rescue them if possible. But we must leave within a day. If there’s any sign of a protracted battle, we must immediately abandon them and evacuate.”
“It seems that’s the only option.”
At this point, Sarah seemed to have been sentenced to her fate, like a fish on a chopping block, at the mercy of others. However, she believed she could still struggle a bit.

chapters.title: Chapter 743: Encounter
chapters.content:
Sarah’s remaining energy was rapidly depleting. Based on the information detected by her sonar system, she still had nearly a hundred meters to go before breaking through this gel-soil layer. Even without interference from the Ji soldiers, Sarah’s energy reserves wouldn’t be enough to sustain her Negative Energy Shield for that distance.
Sarah realized continuing downward was a dead end. She needed to change tactics. The path below had been deliberately reinforced by the Ji race, but the surrounding areas were only partially reinforced, likely no more than fifty meters thick. If she was lucky enough to find an unsealed passage, she had a good chance of escaping this reinforced gel-soil layer.
Once out of here, all she needed to do was continue stalling and avoid being trapped. Eventually, the soil layer she was in would collapse into the depths below.
With her plan set, Sarah immediately shifted tactics. As she fell, her echolocation system activated at full power. Suddenly, the Negative Energy Shield beneath her feet disappeared, and solid ground met her feet, halting her descent.
Though the shield below her vanished, her energy output surged instead. The Negative Energy Shield reappeared, but this time in front of her.
The layers of soil it touched instantly vanished. Sarah pushed off with her legs and charged forward against the shield. The larger contact area caused her energy reserves to drain like air escaping from a punctured balloon.
But now wasn’t the time to conserve energy. When Sarah had pushed the shield forward ten meters and her energy reserves dropped below thirty percent, the obstruction ahead suddenly cleared—she had broken into a tunnel.
In front of her stood a K2N9 unit and two Ji squads. Though she couldn’t see their faces behind their masks, she imagined they must have looked utterly astonished.
Unfortunately, Sarah miscalculated. Her skyrocketing energy output and the noise of her passage through the soil had already been detected by the Ji race. Thus, as soon as she changed direction, Selina sent a warning to the Ji soldiers.
However, Sarah’s speed was extraordinary. Her insectoid body, enhanced by multiple superior genes, was akin to a superhuman in comparison to naturally evolved lifeforms. Though the Ji soldiers received the warning, their physical reactions lagged far behind.But their sluggishness didn’t apply to everyone—or rather, everything. Among these two squads were four mechanical soldiers. The artificial intelligence controlling them made preparations just 0.00001 seconds after receiving the information.
Standing three meters tall, the mechanical soldiers’ Vulcan cannons were already primed by the time Sarah burst through the soil. This outdated weapon had long been retired from the Ji race’s arsenal, but due to the unique nature of this mission, high-damage, high-penetration energy weapons couldn’t be used for fear of harming the Swarm Empress. Thus, these old kinetic weapons were given a rare opportunity to shine again.
The Vulcan cannons spun wildly, filling the narrow tunnel with smoke and the acrid smell of gunpowder—an adrenaline-like scent that excited those who smelled it.
The downside of these old kinetic weapons was their reliance on physical ammunition, which required additional weight. Moreover, with the Vulcan cannon’s extremely high rate of fire, even more ammunition was needed to unleash its full potential.
“Pull the trigger for one second, reload for ten”—this phrase perfectly described the Vulcan cannon. Although it had long been phased out by the Ji race, even back then, their technology had increased its firing rate to over two hundred thousand rounds per minute.
Such a high rate of fire meant that even though each mechanical soldier carried a large external ammunition box on its back, they could only sustain firing for thirty seconds.
But that was enough.
While these outdated kinetic weapons couldn’t harm Sarah in her armored state, the metal storm created by the ultra-high rate of fire acted like a solid wall, crashing toward her.
Under Selina’s computational assistance, the four Vulcan cannons locked down every possible evasion route, forcing Sarah to endure the barrage head-on.
The energetic metal storm slammed Sarah back into the soil layer she had just emerged from. Mud, stones, and sand flew everywhere, and some J-Z-901 took the opportunity to stick to her body. In the blink of an eye, Sarah’s frame had visibly expanded, encased in a thick layer of mud armor, dotted with metal bullet fragments.
Sarah instantly calculated that this situation was untenable. Even if the metal storm could only last thirty seconds, being pinned down for that duration would give the Ji forces enough time to surround her again.
Thus, the Negative Energy Shield reappeared, flashing as it erased the encasing mud, stones, and sand. Though the Negative Energy Shield could only defend a maximum 120-degree arc, Sarah achieved her current effect by toggling it on and off across different parts of her body. However, this not only required immense computational power but also a more robust energy output system to handle the repeated energy surges.
This advanced application of the shield was currently unique to Sarah. Even the original configuration of this system in the Red Fang Breakers couldn’t perform such operations due to insufficient energy cycling system’s strength.
After clearing the encumbrance from her body, Sarah reactivated the Negative Energy Shield in front of her and charged toward the Ji forces through the metal storm. Though it seemed like a long explanation, in reality, from Sarah’s appearance in the tunnel, to being repelled, and then launching another charge, less than two seconds had passed. So brief was this interval that some Ji soldiers hadn’t even closed their mouths in astonishment.
Sarah’s figure flashed past, and the K2N9 blocking the way shattered into several pieces. Sarah grabbed the largest fragment and held it in front of her as she continued charging forward.
In that instant alone, the Negative Energy Shield had dissolved tens of thousands of metal bullets along the way, plus cutting through the K2N9. Sarah’s energy reserves had dropped below twenty percent, and she couldn’t afford to waste a single bit more.
Though the K2N9 was merely an auxiliary device and hadn’t seen an upgrade in tens of thousands of years, it was still occasionally useful for tasks like digging tunnels, so it remained in the Ji race’s arsenal.
Surprisingly, the K2N9’s wreckage proved to be quite sturdy—it was even tougher than the Vulcan cannon’s bullets. Though it couldn’t completely neutralize the bullets’ kinetic energy like the Negative Energy Shield, as a shield, it was adequate.
Even with a shield, however, relying solely on the exoskeletal strength provided by her bio-armor, Sarah still couldn’t advance against the barrage. Therefore, despite her energy reserves dropping below the twenty-percent warning line, she had no choice but to activate the electromagnetic acceleration system.
Fortunately, these abilities were a level lower than her built-in Dark Energy Furnace, making them bearable.

chapters.title: Chapter 744: Annihilation
chapters.content:
In reality, if Sarah had only used basic abilities like electromagnetic acceleration, these functions wouldn’t even cause her energy reserves to drop further. In fact, under the overload operation of her Dark Energy Furnace, her energy reserves were slowly increasing at a gradual rate.
Sarah, holding the K2N9 wreckage and braving the metal storm, was gradually pushed backward by the immense kinetic force. Her feet dragged deeply across the tunnel floor.
However, when the electromagnetic system kicked in, the instantaneous burst of electromagnetic propulsion dramatically increased her power. Sarah immediately reversed her retreat, pushing forward with the wreckage toward the Ji forces.
If only Ji soldiers were present, Sarah would have already eliminated them and escaped. But the presence of four mechanical soldiers had qualitatively transformed this team’s combat capability.
The time bought by the mechanical soldiers finally allowed the regular Ji soldiers to react. They quickly joined the firing line. Their multi-functional rifles were now in energy attack mode. While such attacks could potentially breach Sarah’s bio-armor, according to Selina’s calculations, using them was the fastest way to dismantle Sarah’s defenses.
Indeed, the K2N9’s metal armor couldn’t withstand the attacks from these frontline weapons. After a few shots, several holes were punched through it, and even Sarah, hiding behind it, bore several scorched marks on her body.
With great effort, Sarah hurled the metal wreckage she held. She ducked to avoid a few energy shots, scooped up another relatively intact piece of K2N9 debris, and as she rose, kicked several smaller pieces of metal wreckage lying on the ground.
The kick produced a sonic boom. If Sarah were to participate in any football match, this single kick alone would make her a godlike figure.
The pieces of metal wreckage flew toward the Ji forces like cannonballs. If they got close, they would certainly disrupt the Ji formation.
Two mechanical soldiers redirected their Vulcan cannons. According to Selina’s calculations, since they couldn’t harm the Swarm Empress but could only slow her advance, intercepting the cannon-like metal debris took higher priority.Sure enough, the powerful kinetic projectiles were intercepted mid-air by the kinetic Vulcan cannon rounds. However, what Selina could calculate was based on existing database information; she couldn’t predict beyond that.
With two Vulcan cannons diverted, Sarah’s mobility significantly increased. Though only for a short time, with her superior computational power and reaction speed, Sarah easily seized this opening.
The electromagnetic propulsion reached its maximum output. Sarah’s entire body erupted in a dazzling blue aura, and the air seemed to hum. With a flash of blue light, Sarah surged forward several steps. At the same moment, she was completely enveloped in blue electric light, arcs of electricity emanating dangerous vibes.
Sarah’s transformation immediately alerted the Ji race to a new variable. Although Selina swiftly re-aimed the Vulcan cannons at Sarah, it was too late.
Though Sarah was still several meters away from the Ji forces, they had already entered the electromagnetic field’s range. By this point, Sarah had transformed into a blinding white sphere. Her figure was no longer visible, and the blue arcs of electricity seemed to vanish.
As the energy level continued to rise to its peak, the white sphere suddenly exploded. A powerful energy pulse swept out in all directions like a tidal wave.
The Ji soldiers swept by the pulse erupted in sparks. Numerous weapon systems failed, and even their multifunctional helmet visors short-circuited. The piercing sound of electrical interference nearly ruptured their eardrums without warning.
The pain nerves—a debatable evolutionary or devolutionary trait—caused the intense pain to instantly overwhelm their bodies. They instinctively bent over, clutching their helmets, ceasing fire naturally.
The mechanical soldiers fared even worse, directly shutting down. However, judging by their flickering eyes, they were attempting to reboot and reconnect to the Ji’s network.
Sarah, of course, wouldn’t give them that chance. Despite feeling slightly weakened after unleashing her ultimate move, she quickly stepped forward and dismantled the mechanical soldiers. As for the regular soldiers groaning in pain, Sarah casually grabbed a few high-explosive grenades, pulled the pins, and dropped them at their feet.
Their fate was now up to luck. Don’t blame her for not giving them a chance at survival. A few seconds later, explosions echoed behind Sarah, and the tunnel collapsed into silence.
Although the Ji soldiers’ protective suits could withstand such explosions under normal circumstances, Sarah didn’t know if their material alone could maintain such strong defense after being compromised by the electromagnetic pulse. Even if they could hold up, how long could they last without a functioning air circulation system until rescue arrived? But honestly, why should Sarah care? She wasn’t foolish enough to sympathize with her enemies.
This electromagnetic pulse, though visually stunning, didn’t consume much energy. Its instantaneous output merely slightly exceeded that of the Negative Energy Shield. However, the shield’s continuous consumption was incomparable to this explosive pulse.
Still, this skill was somewhat impractical since Ji equipment generally had good EMP resistance. Sarah had to get close enough to penetrate their defensive systems.
Fortunately, this EMP system required only a small organ to support it, so having this ability didn’t take up much space. Following the principle that more skills are always better, Sarah’s insectoid body was equipped with this ability. Unexpectedly, it proved remarkably effective here.
But essentially, this was a one-time-use ability. Once exposed, given the capabilities of the Ji race’s artificial intelligence, they wouldn’t allow Sarah a second chance to use it in the future.
After clearing the previous Ji squad, there were no more obstacles in the tunnel. A few more steps, and Sarah would be free from this gelatinous area. Escaping here meant achieving more than halfway to success.
Her specially designed insectoid body had strong regenerative abilities. After just a few seconds of rest, the internal damage caused by overloading the electromagnetic propulsion and output had already healed. Sarah regained her combat readiness and immediately quickened her pace. She had already spent nearly ten seconds since exiting the descent tunnel and couldn’t afford to delay further.
Electromagnetic acceleration kicked back in. Within less than a second, despite complex terrain, she could run a hundred meters in the tunnel and escape.
However, the instant she exerted herself, a sudden foreboding arose in Sarah’s mind. She barely managed to shift her body slightly before an enormous force slammed her backward.

chapters.title: Chapter 745: Grave Injury
chapters.content:
Though Sarah Kerrigan’s insectoid body was equipped with various detection organs, compared to specialized large-scale equipment, both the precision and range of her detection capabilities were inferior, especially when it came to energy-based sources.
Thus, when Sarah sensed a distant surge of energy gathering, she immediately foresaw trouble. The location of this energy source contained no Swarm units, ruling out the possibility of it being from her side. Moreover, the position was already beyond her effective detection range, yet she could still sense the overwhelming energy fluctuations, indicating that the source was a massive device.
In this situation, such an occurrence could only mean that the Ji race was targeting her with something extraordinary. Sure enough, in the next moment, Sarah’s hairs stood on end.
Unfortunately, danger struck too swiftly. She had barely begun to evade when the attack arrived. An immense force transmitted to Sarah’s body—a familiar mode of assault. Electromagnetic projectiles over thirty centimeters in diameter, typically used against small warships, were now employed here.
While Sarah’s bio-armor boasted strong resistance to purely physical attacks, everything had its limits. When an attack far exceeded these limits, resistance became irrelevant.
“You’ll kill her!” A roar erupted in the Ji race’s command room.
“Relax. Though this attack far surpasses the target’s endurance limit, based on the bodily data the target has displayed so far, she can completely avoid vital areas.”
“But she will still be severely injured!”
“Enough! I’m tired of this cat-and-mouse game. We only need a living Swarm Empress, not necessarily a fully intact one!”
“But what if she can’t dodge it?”“She will. This attack has already been simulated over a hundred thousand times by Selina. In every instance, the target avoided the vital areas without exception.”
“I hope you’re right.”
“Send our people to check the target’s condition immediately.”
Indeed, the Swarm Empress was gravely injured. At the critical moment, despite her best efforts to dodge the direct impact, the shell fired by the sub-cannon level electromagnetic gun was simply too fast. Sarah managed to evade with only half of her body.
“Hurry! She’s there! She’s alive but severely wounded!” Only ten seconds after the bombardment, new Ji soldiers rushed out from the tunnel.
“My goodness, we must get her to the battleship quickly, or she won’t survive such injuries!” Upon seeing the current state of the Swarm Empress, the Ji soldiers were secretly astounded.
Initially, when their electromagnetic cannon fired, they didn’t believe any individual could survive such an attack. Yet reality harshly taught them a lesson—though the surviving creature looked pitiful.
The Swarm Empress was embedded in the wall. Her right hand, right leg, and a portion of her body had vanished, making her appear extremely emaciated.
“Strange, with such severe injuries, she hasn’t lost much blood!”
“Never mind that, quick, get the cryo-spray!”
The miraculous cryo-spray effectively froze the damaged areas of a living organism, reducing cellular activity and even inducing dormancy without causing cell death. It was a commonly used medical tool on battlefields of advanced civilizations.
“Let’s hope she survives; otherwise, this mission would have been for nothing.”
“Damn, her armor is so hard! Someone help!” One Ji soldier attempted to remove the Swarm Empress’s helmet, but unfortunately, the helmet was seamlessly integrated with her armor.
“We need to remove her helmet to prevent blood from blocking her respiratory tract!”
After several attempts, they ultimately failed.
“Damn it!”
“Don’t worry; the Swarm’s anatomy differs from ours. She’s lost half her body and hasn’t bled much, so she won’t choke herself.”
“Never mind that. K2N9 will arrive soon. Let’s get her down first.”
Carefully, several soldiers pried Sarah off the wall. This operation was successful. One soldier pulled out a metal module about thirty centimeters in length, width, and height from his backpack. After pressing the switch, the module quickly unfolded into a stretcher-like form.
“Be careful!” Just as they were about to lift Sarah onto the stretcher, the ground suddenly shook violently. The unstable soldiers fell to the ground along with Sarah.
“Selina, what’s happening?!” The soldiers asked anxiously. Soon, information appeared on their helmet displays.
During the time Sarah was incapacitated and unable to move, though she was subdued, other Swarm units never ceased their actions. For example, the Burrowing Worms below the battlefield.
After the Burrowing Worms detonated a minefield, causing large-scale detachment in the battlefield area, the Ji race had confined the Swarm Empress within the gelatinous region, so they weren’t overly concerned.
Moreover, near the battlefield, a ring of radiation blocked the Burrowing Worms, causing their attention on them to wane.
Who would have thought that among hundreds of normal Burrowing Worms, the Swarm had concealed more than ten space-based enhanced Burrowing Worms. Under the cover of their kin, they quietly approached the gelatinous soil layer. To achieve this, they even self-decomposed their skin to mimic radiation contamination.
Due to time constraints, the Ji race hadn’t deployed weapons capable of effectively striking the giant units underground. The sudden eruption of the space-based Burrowing Worms caught the Ji race off guard.
Although for the sake of disguise, the two versions of Burrowing Worms looked identical, those now wrapped in blue electric arcs were clearly the high-end versions. They were faster, stronger, more resilient, and immune to radiation contamination.
“Stop them!” The Ji commanders roared, but with frontline soldiers’ individual weapons, facing monsters hundreds of meters long and tens of meters wide felt utterly powerless.
“Take the target away!” The Ji commanders seemed to realize this too. They immediately changed their orders. The Swarm Empress was already in their hands, and they held the initiative. There was no need to confront these giant units head-on.
On Sarah’s side, the fallen Ji soldiers quickly rose and placed Sarah on the stretcher. Unfortunately, the K2N9 arrived late. They had just lifted Sarah onto the vehicle when a giant burst past them.
“Move!” The agile soldiers quickly jumped onto the vehicle, while the wise ones stepped back. But the next second, the ground shook violently. A huge body surged up beneath them, opening a maw like an abyss, swallowing all the soldiers along with the K2N9.

chapters.title: Chapter 746: The Giant Maw
chapters.content:
“The target has been intercepted!” Although the soldiers didn’t have time to sound the alarm, their battlefield recorders captured and transmitted everything up until they were consumed.
“Blast that area open!” By this point, the last of the connecting zones had been breached, causing the entire battlefield to collapse. From above, numerous bottomless pits could now be seen.
“We can’t! Our people are still down there!”
“As long as their suits aren’t hit directly, there’s a fifty percent chance they’ll survive this round of attacks!”
“That will still cause massive casualties.”
“Their sacrifice is worth it; we must complete the mission!”
On the surface, the Ji soldiers had already evacuated. Their detection equipment was hastily reinforced and airlifted away. Due to the rush, a large amount of gear and supplies were left behind.
The underground troops were also notified to either regroup with the K2N9s and K1KN10s or urgently retreat from the battlefield. However, just as they began moving, the bombers tasked with the attack arrived overhead.
The Ji race’s decision was born out of necessity. The Swarm Empress had already linked up with the Burrowing Worms—masters of digging tunnels. If allowed to turn around fully, within minutes, or even tens of seconds, they could dive deep underground. At that point, completing the mission would become exponentially harder for the Ji forces.
A barrage of B5 bombs rained down. According to Selina’s calculations, launching the attack without delay meant the Swarm wouldn’t have time to extract the target from the K2N9. Moreover, with the Burrowing Worms helping to shield her, even concentrated bombardment from multiple B5 bombs wouldn’t kill the target. Other considerations, including friendly troop casualties, were irrelevant.Explosions echoed continuously, and the Ji communication channels were flooded with curses, cries for help, and screams of pain. To avoid undermining morale, the Ji commander had no choice but to block communications from some units.
“Have we located the target?”
“She’s still there, and hasn’t moved far!” When the entire area was swallowed by the Burrowing Worm, the battlefield recorders on the swallowed soldiers lost connection due to the worm’s magnetic field. However, the K2N9 carried a quantum communicator. To avoid harming their Empress, the Burrowing Worm wouldn’t destroy the K2N9.
Indeed, the Ji forces could track the Swarm Empress indirectly by locating the K2N9. The situation was better than expected. Unable to digest what it had swallowed, the Burrowing Worm temporarily lost its ability to dig.
Thus, it could only follow behind other Burrowing Worms, causing slight mobility issues. Its earlier turning maneuver had wasted precious time.
Due to the Ji forces’ swift and decisive response, when the B5 bombs struck, the Burrowing Worm had only completed sixty percent of its reorientation.
After the bombardment ended, the battlefield—which had been reduced to a thin layer of soil clinging desperately together—collapsed entirely, plunging into the depths below. From above, a colossal pit over five hundred meters deep appeared, resembling the maw of an abyss, inducing vertigo at a glance.
Thanks to the enhanced defensive capabilities of space-based creatures, the Burrowing Worm that swallowed Sarah emerged battered and wounded, though only superficially. Even the hundreds of meters of falling caused minimal serious harm.
However, it faced an embarrassing predicament—it couldn’t consume soil while protecting Sarah, thus losing its tunneling ability.
The previously excavated tunnels had already collapsed under the Ji forces’ relentless bombardment, trapping the Burrowing Worm in the deep pit. It could only wait for other Burrowing Worms to carve a path for it.
But since the Ji forces deliberately collapsed the pit, they naturally had countermeasures ready.
“Is the Hercules ready?”
“A few auxiliary modules haven’t been installed yet, and it hasn’t undergone any debugging yet.”
“There’s no time. We can’t give the Swarm any breathing room. Deploy the Hercules!”
The originally clear sky suddenly darkened as clouds gathered, but closer inspection revealed these weren’t clouds—it was a massive warship.
Disk-shaped and over ten kilometers in diameter, this ten-thousand-meter behemoth was something rarely seen by the Ji race, let alone inside a planet’s interior.
Even without any action from the ship, its sheer mass caused gravitational disturbances as it approached the ground. Soil, rocks, sand, dust, grass roots, and leaves defied physics, drifting toward the giant vessel.
By the time it reached its designated position, small storms had erupted around it. During this period, more metal modules continued attaching to its surface. What once appeared enormous—metal blocks over ten meters in length, width, and height—now seemed minuscule in comparison.
“Activate it!” At the bottom of the massive pit, the Burrowing Worm carrying Sarah, aided by dozens of others, began moving again. Half of its head had already burrowed into a newly carved tunnel when suddenly, an overwhelming pulling force seized it, like a giant hand gripping it and attempting to drag it upward.
In the air, a spectacular and dazzling scene unfolded. The “Hercules,” a colossal ship spanning the void, hovered a hundred meters above the giant pit. Its underside opened a circular hatch five kilometers in diameter—a true abyssal maw devouring everything. Compared to this, the Burrowing Worm’s gaping mouth was insignificant.
Dozens of tornadoes, carrying thousands of tons of mud, stones, dust, grass roots, and leaves, surged toward the giant maw, creating an apocalyptic scene. Even at the bottom of the pit, hundreds of meters away from the ship, escape from the immense suction was impossible. The freshly collapsed, loose soil formed the thickest tornado-like column, spiraling upward into the maw.
Even the Burrowing Worm—a behemoth hundreds of meters long and ten meters wide—was rendered powerless before this abyssal maw, akin to an insect being swept away.
Occasionally, Burrowing Worms lost their support as surrounding soil was sucked away, leaving them suspended in the air. Without limbs, these helpless creatures could only await their fate.
Other Swarm combat units, such as Modified Spider Combat Bugs and Heavily Armored Warrior Ants hiding deep underground, were also pulled into the air. These smaller-to-medium-sized units had little resistance against the overwhelming force.
Moreover, this attack was indiscriminate. Ji soldiers, K2N9s, and even the massive K1KN10s were all dragged upward. It remained to be seen what awaited them beyond the giant maw—and whether the Ji forces had prepared measures to distinguish friend from foe.

chapters.title: Chapter 747: Capture
chapters.content:
The “Hercules” was the ace up the Ji race’s sleeve prepared specifically for Sarah Kerrigan. Its advanced instruments could amplify its gravitational pull by hundreds or even thousands of times in a targeted direction. If it landed on the surface of a planet and aimed at its orbiting satellite, it could even trigger a “starfall.”
“Increase the power!” The apocalyptic scene over the battlefield was merely the “Hercules” flexing its muscles—it was far from reaching its limits.
To resist the suction storm, the Burrowing Worms had intertwined themselves into a massive worm ball, significantly increasing their combined weight.
However, as the “Hercules” increased its output, its suction force multiplied exponentially, and the sandstorm grew fiercer. Gradually, the Burrowing Worms were pulled out of the worm ball and sucked into the air.
As the balance tipped, the worm ball could no longer withstand the suction. When only a few dozen Burrowing Worms remained, the entire mass was lifted into the air.
The colossal object, composed of dozens of terrifying creatures each hundreds of meters long, stood out starkly amidst the sandstorm. Seeing it, all the Ji soldiers breathed a sigh of relief.
“The target is inside; she can’t escape now.”
“Be careful not to accidentally injure the target.”
“Don’t worry. The sorting sequence is controlled by Selina—it won’t make mistakes.”
The “Hercules” attack was a classic example of wholesale destruction, indiscriminately pulling in enemy units, friendly units, and even ordinary dust and debris.However, inside, it housed an intricate sorting apparatus. Once objects were sucked in, they were placed in a vast vacuum chamber. Surrounding mechanical claws or small tractor beams would retrieve friendly units or valuable items, while the rest were fed into a large energy furnace for conversion into energy.
For objects that couldn’t be quickly converted but were also deemed worthless, the “Hercules” was equipped with a negative energy generator specifically designed to annihilate such materials.
Though Sarah’s new markers had been removed, the K2N9 she was in still had tracking tags, allowing the Ji race to closely monitor her position. Selina even dedicated a subroutine to keep constant tabs on her.
To err on the side of caution, the Ji race didn’t neglect other targets either. This way, even if the Swarm Empress had been transferred using special means, they wouldn’t be left groping in the dark.
As the worm ball ascended into the air, previously hidden Swarm flying units attempted rescue missions. However, compared to the “Hercules,” their size difference was too great. Even the Vulturehawks couldn’t resist its suction.
Meanwhile, the Swarm forces struggling in near-orbit fired salvos of artillery in support. But the “Hercules” boasted armor thickness and strength beyond imagination, complemented by a negative energy shield.
Though the Ji race hadn’t yet miniaturized negative energy technology to the Swarm’s level, the sheer size of the “Hercules” allowed it to deploy this bug-level defensive weapon. The Swarm space units’ barrage failed to harm it and instead gave the Ji space fleet an opportunity to launch a devastating counterattack.
Thus, the “worm ball” was safely sucked into the “Hercules.” Inside, the long-awaiting sorting apparatus sprang into full operation.
The “worm ball” was placed in a vacuum environment, immediately highlighting differences. Ordinary Burrowing Worms, deprived of their survival environment, began dying struggles, whereas the space-based versions did not exhibit such symptoms.
The struggles caused the entangled worm ball to gradually unravel. Mechanical claws, already on standby, seized the separated Burrowing Worms.
Each Burrowing Worm, including those sucked in earlier, required thorough inspection. Who knew whether the Swarm Empress might have been transferred during their entanglement?
“That’s the one!” The Burrowing Worms were quickly separated. Even the space-based versions retained some combat capability, but this was the Ji race’s home turf—their strongest advantage—and capturing them was effortless.
At the center of the worm ball was naturally the Burrowing Worm carrying the K2N9.
“Retrieve the K2N9 first!” Once this Burrowing Worm was exposed, it received VIP treatment. A containment field enveloped it, neutralizing its resistance. It was then transferred to a separate area, where several laser cutters moved around its body, creating openings through which reconnaissance drones were inserted.
Based on feedback from the drones, non-essential parts of the Burrowing Worm were swiftly excised, confirming that the Swarm Empress wasn’t hiding elsewhere in its body.
Simultaneously, the location of the K2N9 was isolated. Without the magnetic interference from the Burrowing Worm, the battlefield auxiliary AI “Selina” immediately took control of it.
The hatch opened slowly, and the first to emerge were several Ji soldiers. Fully enclosed protective suits allowed them to operate unaffected in the vacuum environment.
“The target is inside!”
These Ji soldiers had performed a great service. The Swarm had indeed attempted to transfer the Swarm Empress but, to avoid harming her, only used small units for attacks. Relying on the K2N9’s decent defenses, these soldiers repelled those assaults.
Subsequently, the Ji race acted swiftly. From the moment the “Hercules” arrived until they were brought here, the Swarm never found another opportunity to transfer the Swarm Empress.
These soldiers truly embodied the saying “a narrow escape brings good fortune.” Their voices brimmed with joy as they promptly reported their situation.
“The target’s condition is unknown. Since we discovered her, she hasn’t moved, but she should still be alive.”
“Due to the visor and helmet obstruction, we couldn’t directly observe the Swarm Empress’s face or inspect her body. However, we’ve applied emergency cryogenic spray to her wounds.”
“Understood. You are the heroes of this mission; your contributions will not be forgotten. Go rest now.” After dismissing the soldiers, who were both relieved and elated, the Ji race’s relevant personnel began examining the Swarm Empress’s condition.
“Activate the air valve!” Upon closer inspection, it became clear that the Ji soldiers, equipped with only basic first aid knowledge and limited tools, had performed only rudimentary treatment on the Swarm Empress’s wounds.
In the vacuum environment, the pressure differential between her body and the surroundings made her injuries potentially fatal. Any breach of the sealed wounds could expel internal tissues.
If the target were to die due to this oversight, their commanding officer would surely make them wish they were dead.

chapters.title: Chapter 748: Doubts
chapters.content:
Time didn’t drag on for long. The vacuum chamber was quickly filled with air, and the pressure was adjusted to match that of the planet below.
As the target’s previously swollen wounds visibly subsided, all the emergency responders secretly exhaled in relief.
“Hurry, transfer her to the medical bay for treatment!”
After a flurry of activity, the Swarm Empress was finally moved to a luxurious emergency room. However, when faced with the severity of the Empress’s injuries, the medical team found themselves at a loss.
The Swarm Empress’s bio-armor presented a challenge. Though heavily damaged, it remained firmly attached to her body. The Swarm’s bio-armor was unique—it wasn’t like the Ji race’s wearable armor. Removing it forcefully would cause severe harm to the wearer.
“Forget about the armor for now. Our goal isn’t to heal her but merely to keep her alive. First, excise some tissue samples for research.”
Initially, the situation here drew close attention from the Ji command center. However, specialized matters were beyond their expertise, and observing simple biopsy experiments wasn’t particularly engaging. They soon shifted their focus elsewhere.
Meanwhile, on the frontline battlefield, the capture of the Empress had driven the Swarm forces into a frenzy. However, this frenzy bordered on suicidal—they clearly lacked the capability to prevent the Ji race from capturing her.
That said, while these Swarm forces faltered, others did not. The Ji race had detected several large-scale Swarm space fleets converging from at least three directions.
Although the fastest fleet had been delayed by Ji traps for five days, only slightly over three days had passed so far. However, according to the latest intelligence, the Swarm forces had begun accelerating recklessly, disregarding their own losses. They were expected to arrive a day earlier than anticipated.This left them with less than a day to retreat.
“The target has been captured; let’s withdraw!”
“Our people are still on the planet.”
“How much time do they need to retreat?”
“At least a full day.”
“Impossible! We have at most 15 hours to start retreating, otherwise we risk being surrounded and losing everything we’ve worked for.”
Retreat wasn’t as straightforward as the initial deployment. Airdropping simply required stuffing soldiers into capsules and ejecting them. Retreating, however, needed transport vehicles to ferry them back to the near-orbit fleet.
Since many soldiers were deployed via drop pods, there were no available return vehicles for them. Those transported by gunships or shuttles had already suffered heavy losses in the first phase due to the unneutralized Swarm anti-air defenses.
Some soldiers were buried under layers of soil, requiring time to excavate. Add to that the wounded, who would occupy more cabin space than usual, and the relentless Swarm attacks—retreating within a single day seemed nearly impossible, let alone within 15 hours.
“We’ll do what we can. Bring back as many as possible. Abandon all equipment—destroy it all to prevent technological leaks.” To safeguard their advanced technology, anything they couldn’t take with them had to be obliterated.
This included vehicles like K2N9s and K1KN10s. As for the mechanical soldiers, they were expendable anyway. Their final value lay in covering the retreat of the Ji soldiers.
The tense evacuation operation began. The original battlefield was in ruins, with layers of collapsed soil burying many Ji soldiers. Rescuing them in a short timeframe using only vehicles like K2N9s was nearly impossible.
Thus, the “Hercules” re-entered the scene. It directly sucked up all the soil within several kilometers around the battlefield, expanding the pit multiple times. Relying on its internal sorting mechanisms, it rapidly rescued the buried Ji soldiers.
However, this meant abandoning the “Hercules.” Due to its size, it lacked long-range travel capabilities. When the Ji race initially arrived, they began assembling this behemoth. After intense effort, it was completed just three days ago.
Dismantling it would require significant time—slightly less than assembly, but still at least two days. With only 15 hours left, even if they couldn’t fully dismantle it, they could salvage its most critical components. But if it participated in the rescue, the Ji race would ultimately have to destroy it, leaving behind a pile of scrap metal for the Swarm.
In the frantic rescue efforts, large numbers of Ji soldiers were saved. Once again, a continuous stream of “caravans” appeared in the sky, ferrying soldiers back to the near-orbit fleet.
Previously hidden Swarm anti-air installations resurfaced, managing to shoot down a few Ji vehicles before being destroyed by patrolling unmanned fighter drones, eliminating any lingering threats to the evacuation.
Mechanical soldiers formed new strongholds, working alongside automated defensive weapons to repel the Swarm ground forces’ final assault. Some Ji soldiers without immediate transport assignments voluntarily joined in to help.
Everything seemed to be progressing as the Ji race hoped. But then, bad news came from the emergency room.
At first hearing, the Ji commanders feared the worst—that the Swarm Empress had died. Upon closer inspection, however, they discovered something else. In an attempt to treat the Swarm Empress, the medical team had excised a small piece of her tissue for analysis. But when they tried to study the sample, it spontaneously collapsed.
This was indeed troubling. While all known Swarm units—combat units and intelligent Swarm alike—possessed this self-destructive trait, the Ji race had always assumed the Swarm Empress was exempt.
According to their records, the Swarm originated as a minor rural tribe that gained access to an ancient inheritance and evolved. The Swarm Empress was supposed to be the first beneficiary of this inheritance. The genetic secrets binding other Swarm units were thought to be shackles imposed by the Empress herself. Yet now, it seemed she shared those same restrictions.
This revelation baffled the Ji race. Did the Swarm hierarchy extend beyond the Swarm Empress? Or was this the price paid by the rural tribe when transforming into the Swarm? Alternatively, was the captured Empress merely an imposter?
Given the Swarm’s prowess in biotechnology, creating an imposter wouldn’t pose much difficulty. Verifying the authenticity of the target had been one of their greatest concerns prior to the mission.
Yet, the secret channels of the Council of Elders confirmed that this Empress was genuine. Now, confronted with this unexpected development, the perplexed Ji race could only report the situation upward.

chapters.title: Chapter 749: Ideas
chapters.content:
The feedback came back quickly, indicating that the Ji race’s higher-ups were closely monitoring the war in real-time. The message was simple—it didn’t confirm whether the captured Swarm Empress was genuine or fake. Instead, it ordered them to return to their lines as quickly as possible and transport the target through the star gate to a designated star system.
Though no specific explanation was provided, it seemed they had gleaned some understanding.
The evacuation efforts accelerated significantly. Ji soldiers waiting for transport began wrapping up their tasks, ensuring all remaining equipment, including weapon remnants, was destroyed.
“Move faster! We’re out of time.” The underground battlefield had indeed been vast, even after contracting the combat zone. Post-battle, many personnel remained stranded in various locations. Even with the “Hercules” assisting in rescue operations, it was impossible to extract everyone within just a few hours.
“We can’t wait any longer. All personnel are to retreat immediately. Those who haven’t been rescued will be classified as missing in action!” Upon the commander’s order, all teams still lingering on the surface began retreating rapidly.
Thanks to the Ji race’s unique organizational structure, soldiers had little camaraderie beyond their squadmates. Thus, even though the commander issued such an unsympathetic directive, dissenters were few.
The Swarm Empress was escorted by a gunship squadron to the near-orbit fleet without incident—a smoothness that felt almost unreal.
However, the Swarm Empress’s condition was concerning. She had been transferred to a more advanced medical bay, but the Ji emergency responders were unable to provide effective treatment.
“How’s the target’s condition?” On the large screen connecting to the rear command room, the commanders inquired. The emergency responders shook their heads.
“Not good. Since she was discovered, the target hasn’t moved at all. Due to our limited understanding of the Swarm, we don’t even know what their vital organs are or where they are located. Consequently, we have no way to monitor her vital signs.”“Is the target still alive?” The commanders’ expressions darkened.
Over ten hours had passed since the Swarm Empress’s capture. Among the Confederation’s two hundred-plus races, under such severe injuries and without effective treatment, only a handful could survive.
“Most likely still alive. The target is still fully covered in her armor. While this prevents us from directly observing her body to assess her condition, it indirectly confirms she’s still alive.”
Upon hearing this explanation, those in the command room nodded silently. The Swarm’s bio-armor was a remarkable phenomenon—it lived symbiotically with its host. If the host died, the armor would lose its vitality.
They believed that the Swarm Empress’s custom armor, though functionally different from the mass-produced versions, wouldn’t deviate from this principle.
But continuing like this wasn’t a solution. Even if everything went smoothly, it would take at least two years to reach the designated star system. Whether the Swarm Empress could endure until then was uncertain.
“Haven’t you thought of any other solutions?”
The emergency responders shook their heads. “We don’t even know the target’s basic anatomical structure, so we can’t provide effective treatment.”
The commanders were at a loss. Different species had varying body structures and capabilities. For most races, the brain and circulatory core were critical—damage to either often meant death. But not for all. Take the Senqi race, for example; their people had two heads, and some mutated individuals even had three or more. Even if critically injured, as long as one head survived, they lived.
Then there was the Haixue race. Their heads weren’t vital organs. Only destroying their mobile circulatory core could kill them, giving them incredible survivability.
Thus, the criteria for assessing injury severity varied greatly between species. Without specific knowledge of their anatomy and data, it was difficult to intervene.
Especially for the Swarm—an expert in biotechnology—they had made countless modifications to their own bodies. Take the Swarm Empress, for instance. She could casually break the sound barrier, toss around K2N9s like toys, and even activate Negative Energy Shields.
While her bio-armor undoubtedly played a significant role, claiming she was physically frail was something no Ji soldier would believe.
Many emergency responders speculated that perhaps the Swarm Empress’s seemingly severe injuries weren’t as dire. According to battlefield records, when she was found, her wounds hadn’t bled much—a situation beyond many responders’ comprehension. Such speculation was understandable.
Perhaps beneath that cold visor, the Swarm Empress was watching their helplessness. But these were mere guesses. They couldn’t gamble—if she truly succumbed to her injuries, who would they blame?
Amidst the silence, one responder suddenly brightened, proposing a novel idea: “Perhaps we should proactively contact the Swarm. I’m sure they wouldn’t want their Swarm Empress to die from untreated injuries.”
At first, the suggestion seemed impractical—they had abducted the Swarm’s Empress and now sought their help for treatment? That would be sheer audacity.
But upon reflection, the idea wasn’t entirely unreasonable. The Swarm Empress’s status within the Swarm was well-known. If she were dead, so be it. But if she were alive, would the Swarm dare watch her perish?
Time was critical. The idea was quickly approved and formalized into a plan. Thus, amidst the Ji race’s frantic retreat and the Swarm’s relentless counterattack, a stern yet peculiar message was broadcast directionally.
This regional broadcast lacked confidentiality—some information might be intercepted by interested parties. However, the Ji race had no alternative means of contacting the Swarm.
Still, this method had its advantages. News of the Swarm Empress would spread among most of the Swarm, making covert schemes harder to execute. Regardless of intentions, the Swarm’s leadership couldn’t be easily manipulated by overt actions. Of course, this was based on their speculations about their own internal dynamics—perhaps the Swarm wasn’t as riddled with intrigue.
Regardless, this approach significantly increased their chances of obtaining information.

chapters.title: Chapter 750: Retreat
chapters.content:
The Swarm’s reaction exceeded the Ji race’s expectations. It was as if they hadn’t received the message at all—business as usual, with no response whatsoever.
“What’s going on?” The Ji side was genuinely baffled. Even if someone wanted to seize power, could they really be so brazen?
“Could it be that the Empress is unpopular within the Swarm? Have they suffered under her for so long?”
“Do you even believe what you’re saying?”
“Why wouldn’t I? Speculation is speculation—even the most absurd things are possible.”
